clue.text: Drink a lot of Spanish wine and turn in

parts.note: to hit the bottle is to drink heavily, so drinking a lot of something is to hit the it
sack is an old name for sherry or other dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A drinker downs plenty of Spanish wine and then goes off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the' comes from the idiom 'hit the bottle', drink heavily; SACK is the Shakespearean word for sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for going to bed for the night.

clue.text: Cooker has nothing for tramp

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface of a stove
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cooker contains nothing at all for a vagrant to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an itinerant homeless wanderer, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Musician beginning to thrill odd chap

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of thrill is used

parts.note: rum is old British slang for strange or odd
Peter is any man's first name, standing for a chap

explanation.surface: A performer starts to excite a peculiar fellow in the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a brass instrument is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Leading man gets new bird

parts.note: the hero is the male lead of a film or play

explanation.surface: A star actor acquires a fresh girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a girlfriend, which is the surface reading; here it is a wading fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a long-legged grey wading fowl.

clue.text: Close relative is turning up with jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A family member appears wearing flashy jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister, the nearest of blood kin.

clue.text: Something to divert traffic round block in German city

indicators.note: the cone goes round, so its letters are split to enclose the other piece

parts.note: a traffic cone is used to steer vehicles round roadworks
a log is a block of wood

explanation.surface: Roadworks cones re-route vehicles around a city block in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Köln on the Rhine, known in English by its French name.

clue.text: Cease control of organ

definitions.meaning: the knob on a pipe organ that selects a rank of pipes

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: halt, and the drawknob that brings a set of organ pipes into play.

clue.text: Source of information for bank robbery

definitions.meaning: the Financial Times newspaper, read across the City, written as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE FT: the Financial Times is the paper bankers read.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the pink financial daily split in two, and stealing.

clue.text: Two big hairstyles on street feature up North

parts.note: a perm and an Afro are both voluminous hairstyles
a perm and an Afro are both voluminous hairstyles

explanation.surface: Two bouffant hairdos are seen on a street in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up North' suggests the north of England, but means the Arctic regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground frozen all year round is a characteristic of the far northern latitudes.

clue.text: Keep Usain Bolt's property?

definitions.meaning: the quality the champion sprinter is known for, speed

explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold, and the quality of being quick, as of a record sprinter.

clue.text: Sadder rock group without energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the band's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Blur is a British band of the Britpop era
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rock band, now drained of energy, is gloomier than ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low, so the comparative means more downcast.

clue.text: Singer makes a buck perhaps after party

indicators.note: the a and deer pieces are placed after the party word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
a buck is the male of the deer, so an example

explanation.surface: A singer earns a dollar or so following a party gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' reads as a dollar, but is a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of ballads, so a singer.

clue.text: Turning over when start of update's imminent

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from update

parts.note: pending means about to happen

explanation.surface: Flipping things around when a software update is about to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: tipping something upside down.

clue.text: Treat badly tropical fish

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of treat are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone mistreats an exotic aquarium fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Infectious fever leaves mark on South American girl

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a Latina is a woman of Latin American origin

explanation.surface: A contagious illness leaves a blemish on a young woman from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for scarlet fever, an infectious disease.

clue.text: Hurtful extract from newspaper

definitions.meaning: an article clipped out of a paper

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: wounding words, and a press clipping.

clue.text: I am having bad feeling about the City, being foolish

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: the bile goes about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: bile is bitterness or bad temper
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone with resentment towards the financial City is acting stupidly.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the financial City.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, it means stupid or idiotic.

clue.text: One puts up with English vicar

parts.note: a rector, like a vicar, is a parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a clergyman from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts up with' reads as tolerates; split it: 'One puts up' is the definition, 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who builds or raises structures, one who erects them.

clue.text: Stick with rune notch carved

indicators.note: carved suggests cutting into new shapes, so the letters are re-formed

explanation.surface: A wooden cudgel is engraved with a rune and a notch.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's baton is a short heavy stick.

clue.text: Arbiter cooked snack

indicators.note: to cook is also to falsify, so the letters of arbiter are fiddled

explanation.surface: A referee prepares a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is a light snack.

clue.text: Soften a medium

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: Tone down a fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic; it is an artist's paint medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-based paint is a painting medium used by artists.

clue.text: Takes snooker shot again, with second dropping in, gets out of trouble

indicators.note: the second drops in among the other letters

parts.note: to cue is to strike the ball in snooker, so to re-cue is to take the shot again

explanation.surface: A snooker player retakes a shot, potting the second ball, and escapes a tricky position.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them, getting them out of danger.

clue.text: Favour being scheduled in routine

indicators.note: the scheduled word goes inside the routine word

parts.note: rote is mechanical routine
set means fixed or scheduled

explanation.surface: A good turn is part of the planned daily routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon badge worn as a token, as a rosette is.

clue.text: A flavouring, free from Spain, for savoury jelly

indicators.note: the flavouring word is freed from the letter for Spain, losing it

parts.note: spice is a flavouring for food
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A seasoning that comes free from Spain is used in a meaty jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Crush on a Turkish official

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl infatuation, a crush

explanation.surface: Someone has an infatuation with an Ottoman dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A title of high rank in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Smith came mostly unstuck in uneven contest

indicators.note: something come unstuck falls apart, so the letters are disordered
most of the word came, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Smith fell apart in a one-sided fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims CAME to CAM; 'unstuck' then scrambles SMITH plus CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pairing of unequal opponents is a one-sided match.

clue.text: Make departure in a university — farewell

indicators.note: the dying word goes inside the a and university letters

parts.note: to die is to depart this life

explanation.surface: Leaving a college with a final goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is used in English for goodbye.

clue.text: Slight indistinctness of speech

definitions.meaning: an insult, as a verb or noun

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an insulting remark, and words running together.

clue.text: Fashionable thinner bust

parts.note: in means in fashion
a solvent such as paint thinner dissolves things

explanation.surface: A trendy paint thinner has gone broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is slang for bankrupt, unable to pay debts.

clue.text: One agreement that is perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A single bargain that is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: as good as could possibly be.

clue.text: Open a beer perhaps

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: Crack open a beer, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a jar' is a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly open, as a door left ajar.

clue.text: Send message to artist, an exciting read

parts.note: to page someone is to call them by pager
J. M. W. Turner was the English painter

explanation.surface: Message a painter about a thrilling book.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book that keeps the reader turning leaves.
